title: A Machine-Checked Reduction of the Riemann Hypothesis to Pólya–Frequency Positivity of the ξ Taylor Coefficients
description:
A formally verified study, in Lean 4 / Mathlib, of the Laguerre–Pólya / total-positivity approach to the Riemann Hypothesis. The Riemann Hypothesis is not claimed. The paper gives Lean-checked conditional reductions whose axiom footprint is only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The central statement is a tightness theorem. Given the classical Pólya–Jensen, Aissen–Schoenberg–Whitney/Edrei and Laguerre–Pólya-closure inputs and the classical converse, all carried as named hypotheses rather than axioms, RH is equivalent to total positivity of the Toeplitz matrix of the sign-normalized ξ Taylor coefficients. The equivalence is classical (stated for ξ by Katkova); the contribution is its machine-checked form, which shows that the single open input is RH-equivalent and cannot be postulated as progress.

The paper also repairs a target-function error: Mathlib's entire completed zeta Λ0 does not have the Riemann zeros, so the program is rebuilt on Riemann's ξ. It records a moment-determinant ladder for Pólya's positive kernel, a Turán-to-Jensen lemma in degree two, and an independent pseudo-Hermitian operator reduction.

Numerically, the paper starts from rigorous FLINT/Arb enclosures of μ0,…,μ120. In ball arithmetic it certifies that all 1816 contiguous Toeplitz minors of order ≤ 16 in that range are strictly positive and that the sequence is strictly log-concave for n ≤ 118. These are consistency checks against known theorems (Katkova's finite-order Pólya-frequency theorem, the Csordas–Norfolk–Varga Turán inequalities and recent infinite log-concavity), not new positivity results.

Version 1.0.0 updates the June 2026 draft. It replaces floating-point cross-checks with ball-arithmetic certification, removes overstated novelty claims about the computation, records that the μ log-concavity item is settled in the literature, adds 2026 related work, and ties every cited Lean theorem to the archived commit c749786 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23187646). The attached supplement contains the certification script and its output.
